data.body:
RP-04 RESEARCH CRITIQUE COMPLETE; DRAFT remains gated on one maintainer decision.

Expanded application census: (1) provider-owned auth capabilities, (2) deployment-owned static adapter inputs, (3) Rebar-owned security material, and (4) non-secret capability/path references. Transient inbound tokens are request-scoped, not configuration. This replaces the earlier generic SecretProvider/keyring/file-precedence idea. The supported design keeps operation snapshots non-secret; injects native pre-client credential/session capabilities into Rebar-owned factories; uses provider-specific non-serializable SecretStr/SecretBytes carriers only for unavoidable static values; and adds no universal secret broker, automatic keyring, or general cloud-secret retrieval layer.

Authoritative checks now include pinned/current PydanticAI, Anthropic, OpenAI, boto3/botocore, Langfuse, OpenTelemetry 1.44, MCP Python SDK 1.29, Sigstore, oauth2-proxy, Git/Git Credential Manager, GitHub/GitLab CLI and CI guidance, Terraform AWS, MCP Atlassian, Airflow Jira, jira-cli, and pycontribs/jira. The convergence is provider/helper/runtime-owned authentication with adapter-local static termination—not a shared get_secret(name)->str protocol.

Subprocess conclusion: os.environ.copy()/ambient inheritance is normal for trusted same-capability children. Rebar should preserve native Git/SSH/AWS/proxy/CA and unknown-variable chains, remove only exact Rebar-declared sibling-secret names, overlay a materialized static value only for its owning child, and never mutate global os.environ. Deployment step/container/service scoping remains the primary boundary; this is containment, not a sandbox. Optional write-only Langfuse/OTLP tracing remains a deliberate no-op on auth/setup failure because it cannot authorize or affect a verdict; security/load-bearing auth remains fail-closed.

Synthetic experiments reproduced current repr/mapping/hash leakage, unrelated bridge credential propagation, OpenTelemetry/MCP startup capture, static restart rotation, and the op-cert global-environment race. The existing ADR 0049 path still fetches SSM once per job, sees a later rotated key, creates mode-0600 tempfiles, and removes them. Interleaved/timed-out workers expose key path and push-off process-wide today; a typed ContextVar candidate isolates simultaneous threads and resets cleanly. Call-graph inspection shows run_job can bind push-off before workspace creation, nest the signer after per-job SSM fetch, and let ensure_opcert_key(), opcert_principal(), and _push_mode() consume the binding without changing GateFn/review_plan/verify_completion/sign_completion_verdict signatures.

Verification: the complete synthetic probe passed; an expanded focused regression set covering tracing, all MCP auth facades, op-cert service core/app/integrity, review-bot token redaction, and bridge-runner boundaries passed 132 tests; Gitleaks 8.30.1 scanned the full .joe-janitor directory with --no-git --redact and found no leaks. Research/read-back/critique artifacts are .joe-janitor/rp04-secrets-research.md, rp04-composition-readback.md, and rp04-adr-research-critique.md.

PENDING CONFIRMATION: preserve ADR 0049 per-job SSM fetch and 0600-tempfile rotation, while replacing only its process-global key-path, principal, and sync-push handoff with the typed context-local runtime binding above. No ADR, epic, stories, or production changes have been created.
